questions.question: In India, CRR is fixed by _______________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Reserve Bank of India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) **is the **share of a bank’s **total **deposit that is mandated **by the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI) **to be maintained with the latter as reserves in the form of **liquid cash**. 
 
• The **current cash reserve ratio **is at **4%, **this will be changed **to 4.5% **from **May 21st**.
 
• Objectives of **Cash Reserve Ratio**:
 
 
• ** Cash Reserve Ratio **ensures that **a part of the bank’s deposit **is with the **Central Bank **and is hence, secure.
 
• Another objective of **CRR **is to **keep inflation under control**. During high **inflation in the economy**, **RBI raises **the CRR to **reduce the amount of money **left with **banks to sanction loans**. It **squeezes **the **money flow **in the **economy, reducing investments and bringing down inflation**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The statutory Liquidity Ratio **(SLR) **is the **proportion **of **liquid assets **to time and **demand liabilities**.
 
• The rate of **SLR **is **18.00%**.

questions.question: Which of the following is the first city in history to host the Paralympic Games for a second time?

The correct answer is __**Tokyo**__.

__
 
• **The Paralympic Games **or **Paralympics**, also known as the **Games of the Paralympiad**, is a **periodic series **of **international multi-sport events **involving athletes with a range of **physical disabilities**, **including impaired muscle power, **impaired passive range **of movement**, limb deficiency, **leg length difference**, **short stature**, **hypertonia**, **ataxia**, **athetosis**, vision impairment and **intellectual impairment**.
 
• There are **Winter and Summer Paralympic Games**, which since the **1988 Summer Olympics in Seoul**, **South Korea**, are held almost **immediately following **the respective **Olympic Games**.
 
• The **Paralympics **has grown from a small gathering of **British World War II **veterans in **1948 **to become one of the **largest international sporting **events by the **early 21st century**.
 
• The** Paralympics **has grown from **400 athletes **with a **disability from 23 countries **in **Rome in 1960**, where they were proposed by doctor **Antonio Maglio**, to **4520 athletes **from **163 National Paralympic Committees **at the **2020 Summer Paralympics**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **International Paralympic Committee **(including Paralympic athletics, Paralympic swimming, Paralympic shooting, Paralympic powerlifting, Para-alpine skiing, Paralympic biathlon, Paralympic cross-country skiing, Para ice hockey, Para snowboarding).

questions.question: Who among the following was the author of the famous work “Sangita Ratnakara”?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sharngadeva**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Sangita-Ratnakara **literally **"Ocean of Music and Dance", **is one of the most important **musicological texts **from **India**.
 
• **Composed by Sharngadeva **in **Sanskrit **during the **13th century**, both **Hindustani music **and **Carnatic music **traditions of **Indian classical music **regard it as a **definitive text**.
 
• It is also called **'Saptadhyayi' **as it **consists **of **seven chapters**.
 
• **Sharngadeva **or **Sarnga Deva **was the **13th-century **Indian **musicologist **who **authored Sangita Ratnakara **– the **classical Sanskrit **text on **music **and **drama**. It is considered to be the authoritative treatise in **Indian classical music **by both **Hindustani music **and **Carnatic music**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lochan kavi **belonged to the **Mithila region, Bihar**, and was also called **Lochan Panḍit**.
 
• **Jaidev **was a **music composer **in **Hindi films**, most known for his **work in films**: **Hum Dono**, **Reshma Aur Shera**, **Prem Parbat**, **Gharaonda **and **Gaman**. He won the **National Film Award **for **Best Music Direction**, **three times **for **Reshma Aur Shera**, **Gaman and Ankahee**.
 
• **Ramamatya **was the **grandson of the illustrious Kallinatha**. He was also the **royal composer and architect **at the **court of king Ramaraja**.

questions.question: Padma Bhushan, Kanak Rele was conferred with the award for her significant contribution to which of the following dance forms?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mohiniyattam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mohiniyattam **is an **Indian classical dance **form that developed and **remained popular **in the state of **Kerala**. **Kathakali **is another **classical dance **form **in Kerala.**
 
• The **dance **is **performed **by **women **in honour of the **Hindu god Vishnu **in his **incarnation **as the **enchantress Mohini.**
 
• **Kanak Rele **is an **Indian dancer**, **choreographer**, and academic best known as **an exponent of Mohiniyattom**.
 
• She is the **founder-director **of the **Nalanda Dance Research Centre **and the **founder-principal **of the **Nalanda Nritya Kala Mahavidyalaya in Mumbai**.
 
• She was **born on 11 June 1937 **(age 85 years) in **Gujarat**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kuchipudi **is one of the **eight major Indian classical dances**. It **originates **from a **village **named **Kuchipudi **in the **Indian **state of **Andhra Pradesh**. **Kuchipudi **is a **dance-drama performance**, with its **roots **in the ancient **Hindu Sanskrit text **of **Natya Shastra**.
 
• **Kathak **is one of the **eight major forms **of **Indian classical dance**. It is the **classical dance **form of **Uttar Pradesh**. The origin **of Kathak **is traditionally attributed to the **travelling bards **in of **ancient northern India **known as **Kathakars or storytellers.**
 
• **Bharatanatyam **is a **major form **of **Indian classical dance **that originated in **Tamil Nadu**. The dance form is also **briefly mentioned **in the **Kannada text Manasollasa **written by **Someshwara III**. It has **flourished **in the **temples **and **courts **of **southern India since ancient times**.

questions.question: Which disease refers to the inflammation of the liver caused by a variety of infectious viruses and non-infectious agents leading to a variety of health problems?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hepatitis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Non-infectious diseases **are **caused **by **factors **such as **genetics**, **malnutrition**, **environment**, and **lifestyle**. Examples of **non-infectious **diseases include **cancer, Alzheimer's disease, and epilepsy.**
 
• **Infectious diseases **are **disorders caused by organisms **— **such as bacteria**, **viruses, fungi**, **or parasites**. Many organisms live in and on our bodies. They're normally harmless or even helpful. But under **certain conditions**, **some organisms **may **cause disease**. Some **infectious diseases **can be **passed from person to person**.
 
• **Hepatitis **means **inflammation **of **the liver**. The **liver **is **a vital organ **that **processes nutrients**, **filters the blood**, and **fights infections**. When the liver is **inflamed or damaged**, its **function **can be **affected**.
 
• **Heavy alcohol use**, **toxins**, **some medications**, and certain **medical conditions **can **cause hepatitis**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tuberculosis (TB) **is **caused **by a **bacterium **called **Mycobacterium tuberculosis**. The **bacteria **usually **attack **the **lungs**, but **TB bacteria **can attack **any part of the body **such as **the kidney**, **spine**, and **brain**. Not everyone **infected **with **TB bacteria **becomes **sick**.
 
• In **pneumonia**, the air **sacs **may **fill with fluid or pus**. The **infection **can be **life-threatening **to anyone, but particularly to **infants, children, **and **people over 65**. **Symptoms **include **a cough **with **phlegm or pus**, **fever**, **chills**, and **difficulty breathing**.
 
• **Diabetes **is **a chronic **(long-lasting) **health condition **that affects how **your body turns food into energy**. Your **body breaks down **most of the **food you eat into sugar (glucose**) and **releases **it into **your bloodstream**. When your blood **sugar goes up**, it **signals **your **pancreas **to **release insulin**.

questions.question: Out of the given four alternatives, select the one that is NOT a constitutional body.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**National Human Rights Commission**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **India**, a Constitutional body is a body or **institute **established by the **Constitution of India**. They can only be **created **or **changed **by passing a **constitutional amendment bill**, rather than an **Act of Parliament**.
 
• The **National Human Rights Commission **of **India **is a **statutory public body **constituted on **12 October 1993 **under the **Protection of Human Rights Ordinance of 28 September 1993**.
 
• It was **given **a statutory basis by the **Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993**.
 
• **Arun Kumar Mishra**, a **former Judge of the Supreme Court **is the **current chairperson of the commission **(11th chairperson of NHRC). 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Finance Commissions **are commissions **periodically constituted **by the **President of India **under **Article 280 **of the **Indian Constitution **to define the **financial relations **between the **central government of India **and the **individual state governments**.
 
• The **Election Commission of India **is a **constitutional body**. It was established by the **Constitution of India **to **conduct **and **regulate elections **in the **country**.
 
• The **Union Public Service Commission**, commonly abbreviated as **UPSC**, is **India's premier central recruitment agency **for recruitment of all the **Group 'A' officers **under the **Government of India**.

questions.question: Kelucharan Mohapatra, awarded with Padma Vibhushan in 2000, was a dancer of which of the following dances?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Odissi**__.

__
 
• **Kelucharan Mohapatra **was a **legendary Indian classical dancer**, **guru**, and **exponent of Odissi dance**, who is **credited with the revival and popularizing **of this **classical dance form in the 20th century.**
 
• He is the **first person **to **receive **the **Padma Vibhushan from Odisha**.
 
• He was **born on 8 January 1926 **and **died **on **7 April 2004**, in **Bhubaneswar**.
 
• **Odissi **is traditionally a **dance-drama genre **of **performance art**, where the **artist **and **musicians play out a story**, **a spiritual message **or **devotional poem **from the **Hindu texts**, using **symbolic costumes**, **body movement**, **abhinaya (expressions), **and **mudras (gestures and sign language) **set out in **ancient Sanskrit literature**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mohiniyattam **is an **Indian classical **dance form that **developed **and remained popular in the **state of Kerala**. **Mohiniyattam **dance gets its name from the **word Mohini **– **a historical enchantress avatar **of the **Hindu God Vishnu**, who helps the **good prevail **over **evil by developing her feminine powers**.
 
• **Kathak **is one of the eight major forms of **Indian classical dance**. It is the **classical dance **form of **Uttar Pradesh**. The **origin **of **Kathak is **traditionally attributed to the **travelling bards **in **ancient northern India **known as **Kathakars or storytellers.**
 
• The **Manipuri Dance**, also referred to as the **Manipuri Raas Leela **is one of the eight major Indian classical dance forms, originating from the state of **Manipur. **The dance form is **imbued with the devotional themes **of **Madhura Raas **of **Radha-Krishna **and is characterized by gentle **eyes and soft peaceful body movements.**

questions.question: What components are often called the building blocks of the body that play a vital role in helping to repair and strengthen muscle tissues after exercise?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Proteins**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Proteins**

 
 
• Of all macromolecules,** proteins have the widest diversity of functions and are one of the most abundant organic molecules **in biological systems.
 
• Because there are **20 different chemically unique amino acids that combine to produce lengthy chains of proteins**, the functions of proteins are **extremely diverse**.
 
• Protein is essential to **our diet because it helps our bodies create and repair new cells**.
 
• For children, teenagers, and pregnant women, protein is also crucial for **growth and development**.
 
• Consumed protein is **converted to amino acids by the body** and then absorbed.
 
• It is utilised in the **development of muscles and organs, production of hormones and antibodies, storage of fat, and production of energy**.
 
• Proteins are commonly called as the building blocks of the body because they play a vital role in helping to repair and strengthen muscle tissues after exercise.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Animal products** such as **meats, milk, fish, and eggs are rich sources of protein**, they can also be found in **plant-based foods** like **some grains, beans, soy, legumes, nut kinds of butter, and legumes**.
 
• **Carbohydrates**
 
 
• **Carbohydrates also called carbs** are one of the** three primary nutrients included in foods and beverages**, along with proteins and fats.
 
• The body converts carbohydrates to **glucose**. The primary **fuel for your body's cells, tissues, and organs is glucose, also known as blood sugar**.
 
• **Grains, such as bread, cereals, and rice**, are typical sources of carbs.
 
• **Providing energy to all of the body's cells** is the main function of carbs
 
 
 
• **​Micronutrients**
 
 
• **Vitamins and minerals **that our body needs in **very small amounts are known as micronutrients**.
 
• However, they have a c**rucial impact on a body's health**, and a lack of any one of them can result in serious, even li**fe-threatening illnesses**.
 
 
 
• **Fats**
 
 
• Fat is the **primary energy storage type in the body** and is used as a fuel source by the body.
 
• A **moderate amount of fat is required in the diet for optimal health** since it performs numerous other vital activities in the body.
 
• Food contains a variety of fats, such as **monounsaturated, polyunsaturated, and saturated fats**. 
 
• **Butter, oil, nuts, meat, fish, and various dairy products **are a few examples of foods that include fats.

questions.question: Which crop grows best in areas with hot, humid climate and requires temperature between 21°C to 37°C with well distributed rainfall or irrigation facilities of about 100 cm?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Rice**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rice **

 
 
• Most people in **India eat rice as their main crop of sustenance**.
 
• After** China, our nation is the second-largest rice** producer in the world.
 
• It is a **Kharif crop** that needs **high temperatures (over 25°C)**,** high levels of humidity, and an average annual rainfall of at least 100 cm**.
 
• It flourishes with the **aid of irrigation in locations with lower rainfall**.
 
• In **Southern and Eastern India, it is a favourite staple cuisine**.
 
• Rice is quickly establishing itself in the **North-Western Plain**.
 
• **Mixed farming (Crops + Livestock)** is ideally suited to rice-growing regions.
 
• **Unpolished rice is very nutrient-dense**. It contains plenty of** calcium, vitamin B, and A**.
 
• These** vitamins are absent** from polished rice.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bajra **

 
 
• Bajra is a **rainfed Kharif crop **of dry and warm climate.
 
• It is grown in areas of **40-50 cm of annual rainfall**. The upper limit is 100 cm.
 
• Bajra can be **grown on poor light sandy soils, black and red soils**.
 
• It is sown either as a **pure or mixed crop with cotton, jowar and ragi**.
 
 
 
• **Pulses**
 
 
• The **edible seeds of plants in the legume family are known as pulses**.
 
• **India is the world's largest producer of pulses** (25 per cent of total output),** consumer of pulses** (27 per cent of total consumption), and i**mporter of pulses** (14 per cent).
 
• It can be cultivated in a **variety of climates, although it favours a mild, cool, and rather a dry climate** with temperatures between **20 and 25 degrees Celsius** and r**ainfall between 40 and 50 centimetres**. 
 
 
 
• **Oilseeds **
 
 
• The **world's top producer of oilseeds is India**.
 
• About **12% of the country's total cultivated area** is dedicated to the cultivation of various oil seeds.
 
• It prefers a** tropical climate with temperatures between 20° and 30°C **and **rainfall between 50 and 75 cm**.
 
• The maximum isohyet for **groundnut cultivation is 100 cm**.

questions.question: How do humans acclimatise at high altitudes where atmospheric pressure is low for normal breathing?

options.text: By decreasing red blood cell production, decreasing the binding affinity of haemoglobin and by increasing breathing rate
By increasing red blood cell production, decreasing the binding affinity of haemoglobin and by increasing breathing rate
By increasing white blood cell production, decreasing the binding affinity of haemoglobin and by increasing breathing rate

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**By increasing red blood cell production, decreasing the binding affinity of haemoglobin and by increasing breathing rate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Acclimatisation**

 
 
• **Acclimatisation** is the l**ong-term adaptation to high altitude**, which is primarily carried on **by an increase in red blood cell production and capillary tissue perfusion**.
 
• At high altitudes, acclimatisation typically **takes 1-3 days**.
 
• The b**ody undergoes a number of adaptations** that enable it to **function with less oxygen **at high altitudes, such as:
 
 
• the** depth of breathing increases **or by increasing breathing rate.
 
• Increased **pulmonary arterial pressure "forces" blood into areas of the lung** that are typically not used when breathing at sea level.
 
• The **body creates more red blood cells to transport oxygen**, as well as more of an enzyme. 
 
• By decreasing the **binding affinity of haemoglobin**.
 
 
 
• In order to reduce the **effects of altitude sickness and to balance out increased urination, it's critical to stay hydrated during acclimatisation**.
 
• Despite acclimation, the **heart rate and ventilation rate both rise when at rest, **whereas the heart rate falls when ** at its highest degree of activity due to the release of oxygen from haemoglobin to the body's tissues**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Altitude Sickness**

 
 
• At sea level, **there are around 21% more oxygen** molecules than usual.
 
• While the **concentration does not change with the increase in altitude but the amount of oxygen molecules per breath and the atmospheric pressure decreases**.
 
• At **12,000 feet (3,658 metres)**, there are around **40% less oxygen **molecules in each breath.
 
• Even while at rest, **your breathing rate needs to increase for the body to receive enough oxygen**.
 
• Continued exposure to **higher altitudes without enough acclimatisation might result in very serious, even fatal illnesses**.

__
 
• **Raju Sundaram ** won the National Film Award for Best Choreography at the 67th National Film Awards.

• 67th National Film Awards

questions.question: In which region of India are Kotli Dun and Patli Dun located?

options.text: Between greater Himalayas and the Shiwaliks
Between lesser Himalayas and Trans Himalayas
Between eastern Himalayas and the Shiwaliks
Between lesser Himalayas and the Shiwaliks

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Between the **____**lesser Himalayas and the Shiwaliks**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Duns **

 
 
• Between the **Shiwaliks and the Lesser Himalayas, there are longitudinal valleys called "Duns."**
 
• The word **"dun" is used locally to refer to a valley, especially an open valley in the Sivalik Mountains or between the Sivalik Mountains and higher Himalayan foothills**.
 
• In **Himachal**, these valleys are known by the **names Patli Dun, Kotli Dun, and Pinjore Dun**.
 
• Between the lesser Himalayas and Shivalik, there are longitudinal valleys that are referred to as** "duns" in the west and "duars" in the east**. 
 
• Unlike normal river valleys, **duns are formed structurally and are covered in rocks and gravel that were eroded from the Shiwalik uplands and the Himalayas**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Longitudinal Valley**

 
 
• An elongated valley known as a l**ongitudinal valley is one that is situated between two nearly parallel mountain ranges in geologically young fold mountains like the Alps, Carpathians, Andes, or the highlands of Central Asia**.
 
• They are frequently used by and **shaped by a later stream**.
 
• When the **Indian plate and the Eurasian plate interacted as a result of folding**, longitudinal valleys known as **dunes** were formed.
 
• They are formed between** Shivalik and the lesser Himalayas**.
 
• The H**imalayan rivers that flow down into the valleys deposit coarse alluvium** there.

questions.question: In which month of 2021 was the Gram Ujala Yojana, aimed at providing high-quality electricity at an affordable cost to villages across the country, launched in Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**March**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gram Ujala Yojana**

 
 
• On** March 24, 2021, the Gram Ujala scheme was introduced in Varanasi **in the Lok Sabha constituency of** Prime Minister Modi by Union Power and Renewable Energy Minister R.K. Singh**.
 
• The government provides the **lowest-priced LED lights in the globe in rural areas as part of the programme for Rs 10**.
 
• In a news statement, the **Power Ministry stated that the high-quality LED bulbs will be provided to rural Varanasi residents for Rs.10** each as part of the Gram Ujala programme by** Convergence Energy Services Limited, an entirely owned subsidiary of EESL- Energy Efficiency Services Limited**.
 
• The main aim of this scheme is to **provide high-quality electricity at an affordable cost to villages across the country**.
 
• According to the official press release, **phase 1** of the programme will distribute **1.5 crores LED bulbs, which will significantly impact the nation's efforts to combat climate change by enabling energy savings of 2025 million kWh/year**.
 
• It will also show **CO2 reductions of 1.65 million T CO2/year**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The programme will only be put into effect in the** 2,579 villages of the five districts of Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, and Karnataka**.
 
• The recipient would be permitted to **exchange** a **maximum of five LED lights **under the programme.
 
• **Carbon credits** have been used exclusively to fund the plan.
 
• The new programme will replace the **incandescent and CFL (compact fluorescent lamp) bulbs now being used by rural consumers with new LED bulbs**. 
 
• Within just two days of its launch, the government programme in **Arrah, Bihar, had distributed 6,150 items**.
 
• Once** rural households submit their incandescent lights** under the Gram Ujala Scheme, **12-watt and 7-watt bulbs with a 3-year warranty will be provided**.

questions.question: Padma Bhushan awardee Ustad Sabri Khan was a ______ player.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**sarangi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ustad Sabri khan**

 
 
• **Indian sarangi player Ustad Sabri Khan **was born on **May 21, 1927**.
 
• He was a member of the **Sainia Gharana**.
 
• The famous vocalist **Mian Tansen, who performed in the court of the Mughal Emperor Akbar, is the root of this Gharana's musical heritage**.
 
• His father, **Ustad Chajju Khan**, continued his **training** after being introduced to the sarangi by his **grandfather, Ustad Haji Mohammed Khan**.
 
• On **All India Radio, **Sabri Khan worked as a** staff artist and performed sarangi with a wide variety of vocalist artists**. 
 
• Ustad Sabri Khan received **numerous honours and awards in recognition of his contribution to Indian classical music**, including:
 
 
• **Sahitya Kala Parishad Award**
 
• **Uttar Pradesh Sangeet Natak Academy Award (1990)**
 
• **National Sangeet Natak Academy Award (1986),**
 
• **Padma Shree(1992) **
 
• **Padma Bhushan(2006) **
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sarangi **

 
 
• A **bowed stringed instrument with a resonator** covered in **skin is called a sarangi**.
 
• Typically, a **single block of wood **is used to handcraft a sarangi.
 
• The **seventeen sympathetic strings on this instrument are constructed of steel, while the four playing strings are made of goat gut**.
 
• The sarangi is a **common instrument in India with numerous regional variations**, but it plays a significant role in **the Hindustani music of North India**.
 
• The **sarangi** is the only musical instrument that can **accurately produce all of the nuances of vocal music, including khayal, dhrupad, khayal, thumri, tappa, ghazal, and even bhajan, with embellishments and intonations**.
